questions.q: A tied column uses 25 mm longitudinal bars, 10 mm ties, and has a least dimension of 450 mm. What maximum spacing controls?
questions.ref: ACI 318-19, Sec. 25.7.2.1 - maximum spacing of transverse reinforcement in tied columns
questions.n: The three ACI limits are 16(25)=400 mm, 48(10)=480 mm, and 450 mm. The least is 400 mm.

questions.q: What joint or discontinuity results when placement is delayed long enough that successive concrete lifts do not intermingle and bond?
questions.ref: ACI 201.1R-11, Sec. 2.3.4 - cold joint
questions.n: ACI 201.1R defines a cold joint as a discontinuity caused by a placement delay sufficient to prevent intermingling and bonding of successive lifts.

questions.q: What is a reinforced-concrete floor in which a solid slab is supported by reinforced-concrete beams or girders?
questions.ref: Concrete Reinforcing Steel Institute (CRSI), Reinforced Concrete Terminology
questions.n: CRSI defines beam-and-slab floor construction as a reinforced-concrete slab supported by reinforced-concrete beams or girders.

questions.q: What is the continuous bar support used beneath bottom reinforcing bars in a slab?
questions.ref: Concrete Reinforcing Steel Institute (CRSI), Reinforced Concrete Terminology
questions.n: CRSI defines a slab bolster as a continuous bar support used to support bottom slab bars.

questions.q: If every tie is secured to all eight longitudinal bars using 0.40 m of wire per intersection, what total tie-wire length is required?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: There are 598 ties with eight bar intersections each; multiplying by 0.40 m gives 1,913.6 m.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.

questions.q: What tie-side dimension should be used for A and B?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: Using the simplified estimating convention , the clear tie side is taken as 500 mm less 40 mm cover at each face.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.

questions.q: For a 400 mm square column with 40 mm clear cover, what tie-side dimension results from the same estimating convention?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: The simplified estimating dimension is 400−2(40)=320 mm.

questions.q: What is the standard term for removing formwork or a mold from hardened concrete?
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology - stripping; see also ACI 347R formwork guidance
questions.n: ACI Concrete Terminology defines stripping as removal of formwork or a mold.

questions.q: Which material consists of a thin cement-mortar section reinforced with several closely spaced layers of wire mesh?
questions.ref: ACI Committee 549, Report on Ferrocement / ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: ACI describes ferrocement as thin cement-mortar sections reinforced by closely spaced layers of wire mesh.

questions.q: What general term applies to transverse reinforcement such as ties, hoops, and spirals in columns?
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: ACI terminology uses 'lateral reinforcement' for transverse reinforcement such as ties, hoops, and spirals in column-like members.

questions.q: At 53 m of tie wire per kilogram, how much tie wire should be allowed?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: The calculated mass is 1,913.6/53 ≈ 36.1 kg; allowing whole kilograms gives about 37 kg.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.

questions.q: Using L = 2(A+B)+20d, what cutting length is obtained for one 10 mm tie?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: Substituting A=B=0.42 m and d=0.01 m gives a 1.88 m cutting length.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.

questions.q: If A=B=0.32 m and the tie diameter is 10 mm, what cutting length results from L=2(A+B)+20d?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: The perimeter component is 1.28 m and the 20d allowance is 0.20 m, totaling 1.48 m.

questions.q: What defect consists of voids caused by insufficient mortar filling around coarse aggregate?
questions.ref: ACI 201.1R-11, Sec. 2.3.7 - honeycomb
questions.n: ACI 201.1R defines honeycomb as voids left because mortar failed to adequately fill spaces among coarse aggregate particles.

questions.q: What term describes concrete having a high cement content?
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: ACI Concrete Terminology defines rich concrete as concrete of high cement content.

questions.q: What reinforcement arrangement uses bands parallel to two adjacent slab edges and also along both diagonals?
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: ACI terminology defines four-way reinforcement as bands parallel to two adjacent edges and both diagonals of a rectangular flat slab.

questions.q: What is the primary placing function of closed column ties?
o: To hold and laterally restrain the longitudinal bars
questions.ref: Concrete Reinforcing Steel Institute (CRSI), Reinforced Concrete Terminology
questions.n: CRSI defines column ties as reinforcing bars bent into closed or related shapes for holding column vertical bars in place.

questions.q: How many closed ties are required for all 26 columns?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: Each column requires 23 ties, so 26 columns require 26×23 = 598 ties.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.

questions.q: Which value governs the maximum vertical spacing of the lateral ties?
questions.ref: ACI 318-19, Sec. 25.7.2.1 - maximum spacing of transverse reinforcement in tied columns
questions.n: ACI 318 limits the spacing to the least of the three governing quantities. Here, 16(20)=320 mm, 48(10)=480 mm, and the least section dimension is 500 mm.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.

questions.q: What weak layer can form when cementitious material and aggregate fines are carried by bleeding to a surface?
questions.ref: ACI 201.1R-11, Sec. 2.3.9 - laitance
questions.n: ACI 201.1R describes laitance as a weak residue derived from cementitious material and fines, often carried by bleeding.

questions.q: Which concrete property is strongly related to the selected water-cementitious materials ratio?
questions.ref: ACI 211.1 - relationship of water-cementitious materials ratio to concrete compressive strength
questions.n: ACI 211.1 explicitly uses the relationship between water-cementitious materials ratio and compressive strength in mixture proportioning.

questions.q: Where should shrinkage-control reinforcement sit in a slab on ground for best effect (ACI 360R)?
o: At the bottom face of the slab
About 1/3 of the depth from the top
questions.ref: ACI 360R-10, Sec. 9.3.3; ACI 223R - reinforcement location in shrinkage-compensating slabs
questions.n: ACI 360R notes that reinforcement position is critical and cites ACI 223 recommending placement about one-third of the slab depth from the top.

questions.q: Which reinforcement addition is commonly used in small quantities to reduce plastic-shrinkage cracking?
questions.ref: ACI 544.3R-08 and ACI 544.1R - fiber-reinforced concrete and plastic-shrinkage crack control
questions.n: ACI guidance identifies synthetic microfibers as a common means of controlling early-age plastic-shrinkage cracking.

questions.q: If 6.00 m commercial bars are used, approximately how many bars are required when each 1.88 m tie is cut from whole bars?
questions.ref: Max B. Fajardo Jr., Simplified Construction Estimate - Metal Reinforcement: Post and Column Reinforcement / Lateral Ties
questions.n: One 6.00 m bar yields three 1.88 m ties. The 598 required ties therefore need ceil(598/3)=200 commercial bars.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.

questions.q: Using the governing spacing, how many closed ties are required along one 7.00 m column if ties are provided at both ends?
questions.ref: ACI 318-19, Sec. 25.7.2.1 - maximum spacing of transverse reinforcement in tied columns
questions.n: A 7.00 m height at a maximum 0.32 m spacing requires 22 spaces after rounding upward, which means 23 tie levels.
questions.scenario: A building has 26 tied columns, each 500 mm × 500 mm and 7.00 m high, with eight 20 mm bars, 10 mm ties and 40 mm clear cover. Tie wire is 0.40 m per bar intersection (53 m per kg); ties are cut from 6.00 m bars.
